blindSummary:
This unit bundles the country's two most protective municipal measures for transgender people with two of the six highest-victim regions in the national monitoring dataset. Its largest city operates the country's first chosen-name registry (preferred name on civic documents, transport subscriptions and staff badges), and another major city runs an alias-name scheme at the town hall and public libraries - practical tools that determine whether a gender-nonconforming visitor is humiliated at a ticket window or not. Against this, two of its constituent regions are named as high-violence areas; a 28-year-old trans woman was found dead in a town of the unit (Oct 2025), linked to a series of robberies targeting vulnerable people, and far-right militants gave fascist salutes along a Pride route in the unit (Sept 2025).

The institutional responses are notably good: the national gendarmerie's scientific branch produced prompt charges with wiretaps and confessions in the killing; the police's political-crime branch moved pre-emptively at the Pride event and stopped trouble before it started. One constituent region's 2015 "natural family" motion and rejection of WHO sexuality-education standards are dated climate signals with no visitor-facing enforcement mechanism.

On balance, the violence concentration is real for a traveller, but the protective registries and the quality of institutional responses partly offset it. Among the country's units, this one has no landmark transphobic-motive conviction - that is recorded in another unit - but it has more practical visitor-facing protections and more documented violence; and unlike a neighbouring unit with similar numbers, its protective measures are concrete and used, not merely symbolic motions.
